facts.text: The male magpie-lark has a black throat and a white eyebrow, while the female has a white throat.
facts.quote: the female has a white throat, the male a black throat and a white "eyebrow".

facts.text: The magpie-lark grows to 25 to 30 cm long, about the same size as a European common blackbird.
facts.quote: a small to medium size bird, reaching 25 to 30 cm (9.8 to 11.8 in) long when fully grown, or about the same size as a European common blackbird

facts.text: Magpie-larks are one of only about 200 bird species worldwide that sing in duet, with partners singing half a second apart.
facts.quote: one of the 200-odd species of bird around the world that are known to sing in duet; each partner producing about one note a second, but a half-second apart, so that humans find it difficult to tell that there are actually two birds singing, not one.

facts.text: Pairs sing duets together to defend their territory, and sing most vigorously at strangers rather than familiar neighbours.
facts.quote: the duet singing is now known to be cooperative: pairs sing together to defend their territory. Magpie-larks sing more vigorously in response to duet calls from other birds than they do to the call of a single rival, and more vigorously still if the callers are strangers

facts.text: The magpie-lark fearlessly attacks much larger birds, including magpies, ravens, kookaburras and even the wedge-tailed eagle.
facts.quote: will fearlessly defend its territory against larger species such as magpies, ravens, kookaburras, and even the wedge-tailed eagle.

facts.text: Magpie-larks sometimes attack their own reflections in mirrors and windows, mistaking them for rival intruders.
facts.quote: They are also known to attack mirrors, windows and other reflective surfaces in which they mistake their reflection for an intruder into their territory.

facts.text: Both parents incubate a clutch of three to five eggs, which hatch after up to eighteen days.
facts.quote: Both parents incubate a clutch of between three and five eggs. Incubation of eggs takes up to eighteen days

facts.text: The magpie-lark lives across almost all of Australia except Tasmania, as well as southern New Guinea and Timor.
facts.quote: occupying all parts of Australia except for Tasmania and some of the inland desert in the far north-west of Western Australia, and appears to have adapted well to the presence of humans. It is also found in southern New Guinea and on the island of Timor.
